transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, honestly, what finally pushed me to come in is... my shoulders and neck just stay clenched all day. It's like I'm constantly bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. You know how the principal always walks in right when the kids are acting up? Little Tommy threw paint across the room last Tuesday, right on the new rug. It's a nice rug, too, one of those alphabet ones with the animals, and they're not cheap. Anyway, by the time evening rolls around, my jaw aches so badly I can hardly even enjoy playing my guitar. I have this beautiful vintage Gibson, picked it up at an estate sale a few years back. The guy selling it didn't even know what he had... but yeah, the tension is just too much lately.
Do you think the tension in your shoulders and neck is related to stress or anxiety from work?

Oh, absolutely. It's definitely the stress. I mean, my mind just doesn't stop, it just keeps circling. I'll be sitting there and suddenly I'm agonizing over whether a small mistake in a story-time activity means I shouldn't be trusted with children anymore. Like last week, I accidentally skipped a page in *Make Way for Ducklings*. Have you read that? It's a classic, set in Boston. My sister actually lives in Boston, right near the Public Garden where those little bronze duck statues are. She's a real estate agent, doing very well for herself, the housing market there is just crazy right now... 

But anyway, I start thinking I've completely ruined my reputation with the parents over something tiny like that. They all have these group texts now, you know how it is. And if they complain and I lose my position, I just spiral into wondering if I'll ever get hired again anywhere else. I'm 53, so then I start panicking about whether my retirement is just slipping away entirely. I always wanted to get a little cabin up in the Adirondacks when I retire. My grandfather had a place up there, built it himself back in the 70s. It always smelled like pine needles and old coffee, and we'd go out early fishing for trout... but yeah, my brain just jumps from one awful scenario to the next like that all day, and my neck just takes the brunt of it.
Are you finding it difficult to enjoy or participate in activities outside of work due to your tension and anxiety?

Well, yeah, it's... it's definitely bleeding into everything else. I mean, my whole life feels like it's on hold. I've been trying to find a new position, but I've missed application deadlines because I just stare at the forms, terrified I'll fill them out wrong. And the interviews I did manage to get? I just stumbled through them. I was sweating, losing my train of thought. It's embarrassing. I used to be so good at interviews. I remember when I interviewed for my first teaching job, back in the 90s. The principal asked me what my teaching philosophy was, and I quoted Mr. Rogers. Fred Rogers, you know? He was such a gentle soul. I met him once, actually, at a public television event. He was exactly the same in person as he was on TV. Wore the sweater and everything. I think it was a red one that day... 

But anyway, yeah, I've even stopped volunteering for the weekend story-time at the local library unless someone else handles all the planning. I just can't take the pressure of organizing it. The library is a great place, though. It's one of those old Carnegie libraries, built with the original stone. They have this amazing stained glass window in the reading room. I used to spend hours in there just looking at the light coming through... but honestly, the anxiety is just keeping me from getting back into the classroom in any reliable way. I just can't seem to get my feet under me.
Is there anything besides work that you find yourself worrying about excessively?

Besides work? Um... no, not that I've really noticed. I mean, my brain is so full of the school stuff, I don't think there's room for much else. Like, my house is fine, my health is fine. I actually just had the gutters cleaned out on Tuesday. The young man who came out to do it, Jimmy, he was actually in my kindergarten class... gosh, it must have been twenty-five years ago now. Time just flies, doesn't it? 

I remember he used to try to eat the paste during arts and crafts. We used that minty-smelling white paste back then, you know the kind? It came in those little plastic tubs with the brush built right into the lid. They don't let you use that anymore, it's all washable purple glue sticks now, which makes a lot more sense, I suppose, much less mess on the tables. But Jimmy turned out just fine, owns his own roofing and gutter business now. He has this big silver truck with his face painted right on the side of it, grinning holding a ladder... 

But, um, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, worrying about other things. No, not really. It's pretty much just the teaching and the interviews that keep me tied up in knots.
Do you often experience physical symptoms like a racing heart or sweating when you're not thinking about work or interviews?

Physical symptoms? Um... like sweating or a racing heart when I'm not thinking about work? No, not really. I don't think so. It's really just the school stuff that sets it off. Like I said, the rest of my life is pretty quiet. I actually try to keep it that way, you know? Keep things simple. I like to sit out on my back porch in the evenings. I have these two big oak trees in the backyard, must be at least eighty years old. They drop so many acorns in the fall, it's like walking on marbles back there. The squirrels just go absolutely crazy for them. 

I've got this one squirrel, I swear he's missing half an ear, probably got into a scrap with a neighborhood cat or something. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she has this big orange tabby named Marmalade. He's a menace, really, always prowling around the fence line. Mrs. Gable is a sweet lady, though. She makes the most incredible rhubarb pie every spring. She uses the rhubarb right from her own garden. I tried growing rhubarb once, back when I first bought the house, but I think I planted it in the wrong spot. It needs a lot of sun, and my yard gets so much shade from those oaks... 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, the physical stuff. Yeah, if I'm not thinking about the classroom or trying to find a job, I don't really get the racing heart or the sweating. It's just... it's just the work stuff that does it to me.
Do you ever feel anxious or worried when you're not thinking about work or anything specific, just a general feeling of anxiety?

A general feeling of anxiety? Um... no, I wouldn't say that. If my mind isn't on the classroom or the job hunt, I'm usually perfectly fine. Like yesterday, I went down to the grocery store to pick up a few things, just totally relaxed. I was wandering the produce aisle, looking at the apples. They have so many varieties now, don't they? Honeycrisp, Gala, Fuji... I remember when it was pretty much just Red Delicious, Granny Smith, and maybe Macintosh if you were lucky. 

Macintosh make the absolute best applesauce, by the way. My grandmother used to make it from scratch. She had this heavy, cast-iron hand-crank peeler that clamped right onto the edge of the kitchen counter. You'd turn the little wooden handle and it would peel the whole apple in one long, continuous ribbon. I used to be so mesmerized watching that when I was a little boy... we'd take the long peels and throw them out in the yard for the birds, though looking back, I'm not actually sure birds eat apple peels. Crows might. Crows are incredibly smart, you know. I saw a documentary on PBS that said they can recognize human faces and even hold grudges. Imagine that, a bird holding a grudge against you because you didn't give it a peanut or something... 

But, wait, I'm sorry, I lost the thread again. General worry, right? No, I don't really get that out of nowhere. It always traces back to the school stuff for me.
Do you ever feel anxious when you're alone in a quiet place with nothing to do?

Anxious when I'm alone in a quiet place? Um... no, I don't think so. If I don't have anything to do, and I'm just sitting by myself, I'm usually pretty calm, as long as I'm not thinking about lesson plans or whether I'll have a job next year. I actually like the quiet. I have this nice armchair in my living room, it's a recliner, upholstered in this soft, dark blue corduroy. You don't see corduroy furniture much anymore, do you? It was so popular back in the seventies and eighties. 

My parents had a whole matching living room set in this burnt orange corduroy. Sofa, loveseat, and an armchair. It was incredibly comfortable, but if you sat on it wearing shorts, it would leave those little parallel lines pressed right into the back of your legs. We had this thick, shaggy brown carpet too, the kind you had to use a special rake on to keep it looking nice. I remember my dad out there on Saturday mornings, literally raking the living room rug. It seems so silly now, but that was just what you did. He'd put on his favorite record, usually Jim Croce or maybe Gordon Lightfoot, and just rake away. "The Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald," that's a haunting song, isn't it? It always gave me the chills when I was a kid...

Oh, I'm sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? Drifting off. You asked about being alone in the quiet. But yeah, no, I don't get anxious just from the quiet. It's really only when my mind wanders back to work stuff.
Do you feel anxious when you're interacting with people outside of a work or interview setting?

Interacting with people outside of work? Um... no, not really. If I'm just chatting with folks around town, I'm perfectly fine. Like a couple of days ago, I was down at the local hardware store to pick up some wood glue and I ended up talking to the owner, Phil, for a good twenty minutes. He's a great guy. His shop is one of those old-fashioned ones, you know? The kind with the creaky wooden floors that smell like sawdust and... I don't know, machine oil and fertilizer? 

I love that smell. It reminds me of my grandfather's garage. He was a mechanic, mostly worked on old Fords. He had this beautiful 1956 F-100 pickup truck, cherry red. He'd spend hours on a Sunday afternoon just polishing the chrome on the front bumper. You don't see chrome like that on cars anymore, do you? Now everything is fiberglass and plastic. It's a shame, really. I mean, I understand it's for fuel efficiency and safety, but those old cars just had so much character. They had a real weight to them. When you shut the door, it made this incredibly satisfying, solid thud. Not like that tinny little click you get when I close the door on my Civic...

Oh, goodness, I've done it again, haven't I? I just start talking and my brain goes on a little vacation. I'm sorry. What was it... oh, being around people. Right. No, talking to Phil or anyone else doesn't make me nervous at all. As long as they aren't asking me about lesson plans or the job market, I'm completely fine chatting with anyone.
Do you think you would feel anxious if you were to retire from teaching tomorrow?

Retire tomorrow? Oh, gosh. Um... no, I think if I just retired and didn't have to worry about teaching anymore, I'd probably feel a huge sense of relief, honestly. The anxiety would probably just vanish. If I didn't have to think about state standards or parent-teacher conferences... 

You know, parent-teacher conferences have changed so much. When I first started, parents would just come in, we'd chat for ten minutes, maybe look at some finger painting, and that was it. Now, they come in with these massive binders and spreadsheets tracking their four-year-old's developmental milestones. Spreadsheets! For kindergarten! I had a father last year ask me about my pedagogical approach to emergent literacy. I just stared at him. I mean, we're learning the alphabet and how to not eat the paste, you know? 

Speaking of paste, do you remember that old white paste in the little plastic tubs with the brush attached to the lid? It had that very distinct, almost minty smell. Some kids used to actually eat it. I never understood that. It didn't taste like mint, I can tell you that much. Not that I made a habit of eating it, but... well, you're a kid, you try things once. Like those little wax bottles with the colored sugar water inside. You'd bite the top off and drink the juice, and then you were supposed to chew the wax like gum. It was terrible gum. It just crumbled in your mouth...

Wait, what were we talking about? Retiring? Right. Yeah, no, if I could just walk away from all the school stress tomorrow, I think I'd be perfectly fine. I'd probably just sit in my corduroy chair and read a book. No anxiety at all.
Do you think you've ever had a period in your life where you felt anxious or worried for no specific reason at all?

Anxious for no reason at all? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, my worry is always attached to something, you know? Usually work. I can't think of a time when I was just sitting there feeling nervous about absolutely nothing. There's always a cause, like... well, like the time they decided to change the entire curriculum right before the school year started. 

Oh, that was a disaster. They brought in these consultants from some educational think tank out in California. These people had never spent a day in a classroom with actual five-year-olds. They kept using words like "synergy" and "holistic paradigm shifts." I remember thinking, "Lady, if little Tommy throws up his chocolate milk on the reading rug, what's your holistic paradigm for cleaning that up?" 

Chocolate milk, though... they actually banned it in our cafeteria a few years ago. Said there was too much sugar. Which, I suppose is true, but the kids were devastated. I remember when I was in school, getting chocolate milk on a Friday was the highlight of the week. It came in those little cardboard cartons that were impossible to open properly. You always ended up tearing the spout and having to drink it out of this mangled, soggy hole. And the straws! Those flimsy little plastic straws that would crack if you bent them too far. We used to try to make chains out of them. If you pinched the end of one, you could slide it into the next one...

I'm sorry, I'm rambling again, aren't I? It's just so easy to get caught up in memories. But to answer your question... no, I don't think I've ever just been anxious out of the blue. It's always tied to something specific, almost always school.
Do you feel anxious when performing your daily routines, such as when you're playing your guitar or volunteering at the library?

Playing my guitar or volunteering? Um, yeah, actually. I try to just focus on the chords, or sorting the books, but my mind just won't stop. I'll be sitting there tuning the A string on my guitar, and my mind keeps circling from whether I'll ever get hired again to whether I've ruined my reputation with parents. 

Parents talk, you know? They have those local Facebook groups now. I remember when parents just called each other on landlines. We had this avocado green rotary phone hanging on the kitchen wall when I was a kid. The cord was about twenty feet long, so my mother could stretch it all the way into the dining room while she was cooking. It got so tangled up over time, it looked like a giant green corkscrew. You'd have to unplug the handset and let it dangle in the air just to let it spin itself out. I used to love watching it spin... 

Oh, I'm sorry. The library. Right. Yeah, even when I'm volunteering there, the worry just keeps going. I'll be shelving books and worrying about whether retirement is slipping away. And then I'll be reading to the toddlers, and I'll start thinking about whether a small mistake in a story-time activity means I shouldn't be trusted with children anymore. 

Which is ridiculous, I know. It's just a book. Usually I read them *The Very Hungry Caterpillar*. That book always makes me so hungry, honestly. He eats a piece of cherry pie and a sausage on Saturday. Have you ever had a really good homemade cherry pie? The kind with the thick lattice crust and the coarse sugar sprinkled on top? My aunt used to make one that was just... well, it was incredible. She grew her own cherries in the backyard...
Do you feel anxious when performing routine tasks like grocery shopping or running errands?

Grocery shopping? Er... well, no, I don't think so. I mean, I just go in, get my things, and get out. I don't really feel anxious about the act of buying milk or anything. I usually go to that big supermarket over on 4th Street. 

Have you seen the produce section there lately? They have these misters that spray the vegetables every few minutes. It sounds like a thunderstorm is starting, just this low rumble and then *psshhhhh*. I always end up getting my sleeve wet when I reach for the cilantro. And they have so many kinds of apples now. Honeycrisp, Fuji, Gala, Pink Lady... when I was growing up, you had red apples and green apples. That was it. Red Delicious, which were always mealy and not delicious at all, and Granny Smith. My grandmother used to make applesauce from the Granny Smiths. She had this hand-cranked contraption that peeled and cored the apple all at once. You just stuck the apple on the prongs and turned the handle. It was fascinating to watch the peel come off in one long, continuous ribbon. I used to try to see how long of a ribbon I could get without it breaking...

But, um, anyway, errands. No, I don't think running errands makes me anxious. I just do what I need to do. It's really just the school stuff that gets to me.
Do you ever feel anxious in social situations that are not related to work or teaching?

Social situations? Like parties or... hanging out with friends? No, not really. I mean, I don't go out all that much, but when I do, it's fine. I don't get worked up about just being around people. I went to a barbecue last weekend at my neighbor's house. Bob. He's got this massive smoker in his backyard. It looks like a small submarine just sitting there on the patio. 

He was smoking a brisket for, I don't know, fourteen hours or something ridiculous. He uses hickory wood, which smells amazing, but it gets into everything. My jacket still smells like a campfire. I remember going camping when I was in Boy Scouts. We went up to the state park, and it rained for three days straight. We couldn't get a fire going to save our lives. We ended up eating cold baked beans out of the can and those little Vienna sausages. Have you ever actually looked at a Vienna sausage? They're terrifying. They look like little pale fingers packed into tin water. We used to dare each other to drink the water they came in. Tommy Henderson actually did it once for a dollar. He threw up behind the scoutmaster's tent about ten minutes later. 

But, uh, no, I don't feel anxious just hanging out with people. The barbecue was nice. We just stood around talking about lawn care, mostly. Bob is obsessed with his grass. He dethatches it twice a year...
Do you think you would feel anxious if you were in a completely different profession or career?

A different profession? Hmm... I don't know, maybe? I mean, I've been teaching little kids for so long, I can't really imagine doing anything else. It's just who I am at this point. I've got my master's in early childhood education, so I'm pretty locked in. 

I guess I could have been a baker. I always liked the idea of getting up before the sun and making bread. There's this bakery downtown, right on the corner of Elm and 5th, and if you walk by there at 4:00 AM, the smell of yeast and warm flour just fills the whole block. They make these incredible sourdough loaves. Sourdough is tricky, you know. You have to keep the starter alive. It's almost like having a pet. My friend Sarah had a starter she kept alive for seven years. She named it Clint Yeastwood. She used to talk to it while she fed it flour and water. She swore it made the bread rise better if you said encouraging things to it. 

I tried making sourdough once during a snowstorm a few years ago. We got two feet of snow overnight, and everything was shut down. The plows didn't even come down our street until the next afternoon. I spent the whole morning shoveling just to get to my mailbox. The snow was that heavy, wet kind that breaks your back. My shovel actually snapped right in the middle of the driveway. I had to finish clearing it with a garden spade. It took me three hours... 

But, uh, what were we talking about? Oh, a different career. Right. I mean, honestly, I'm not sure. I haven't really thought about doing anything else, so I don't know if I'd be anxious or not. I've just been a teacher for so long.
Do you ever wake up feeling anxious without any particular reason or thought in your mind?

Wake up anxious for no reason? Um... no, I don't think so. Usually, if I wake up feeling anxious, it's because I'm already thinking about something specific, like a parent-teacher conference or if I forgot to prep the craft materials. I don't really just wake up in a panic out of nowhere. 

I do wake up early, though. I'm usually up by 5:30. I like the quiet before the neighborhood gets moving. I make my coffee—I use a French press now. I gave up on the drip machine after it leaked all over the counter for the third time. The French press makes a much better cup anyway, as long as you get the grind right. If it's too fine, you end up with all this sludge at the bottom of your mug. It's like drinking mud. 

I buy my beans from this little roaster down by the river. They have a Sumatra blend that is just fantastic. The guy who runs the place, Dave, he roasts them right there in the shop. You can hear the beans cracking when you walk in. He told me once that coffee beans actually pop like popcorn when they roast. First crack, second crack... it's a whole science. Dave used to be an engineer before he started roasting coffee. He built his own roasting machine out of an old oil drum and some washing machine parts. It's the craziest looking thing, all exposed wires and duct tape, but it works perfectly. He's always tinkering with it. Reminds me of my dad. My dad was always fixing things that weren't really broken. He took apart the toaster once just to see how the heating elements worked, and we had to toast our bread in the oven for a week because he couldn't remember how to put the spring mechanism back together...

But, um, anyway, waking up anxious. No, I don't think I do that. Unless I'm dreaming about work, I guess.
Can you think of any situation outside of work or teaching where you feel anxious without having a specific worry or thought in mind?

Outside of work? Without a specific thought in mind... um, no, I can't really think of anything like that. If I'm feeling anxious, there's almost always a reason attached to it. Like, if I'm driving, I might get anxious, but that's because I'm worried about the car breaking down. 

I drive this older Volvo station wagon. It's a great car, built like an absolute tank, but the heater core is going out. I took it to my mechanic, Sal, a couple of weeks ago. Sal's shop is over on 9th, right next to that old bowling alley that shut down. Have you been over there lately? They're turning the bowling alley into one of those indoor trampoline parks. I don't understand those places. It just seems like a giant warehouse designed for kids to sprain their ankles. 

One of my kindergarteners, little Leo, went to a birthday party at a trampoline park last month and came to school on Monday with a bright green cast on his arm. He was so proud of it, though. We spent half of recess just letting the other kids sign it with washable markers. I had to draw a dinosaur on it because he's obsessed with T-Rexes right now. He knows all the scientific names, too. It's amazing what a five-year-old can memorize when they actually care about the subject. He corrected me the other day when I called a Brachiosaurus a Brontosaurus. He just looked at me and shook his head like I was the most disappointing adult he'd ever met... 

But, uh, sorry. What were you asking? Oh, feeling anxious for no reason outside of work. Right. No, I don't really get that. There's always something specific on my mind if I'm worrying.
Can you recall any instance where you felt anxious without thinking about work, teaching, or any specific problem?

Without thinking about work, teaching, or a specific problem... no, not really. I mean, if I'm anxious, there's always a reason. Like, I might get anxious at the grocery store, but that's because I'm worried they're out of the specific brand of dog food my golden retriever needs. He's got a sensitive stomach. 

His name is Barnaby. We adopted him from a rescue up in the county. They found him wandering near an old barn, which is how he got the name. He's the sweetest dog, but he has to eat this specialized salmon and sweet potato kibble, or he just makes a mess of the living room rug. It's an expensive rug, too. It's one of those Persian ones my wife inherited from her grandmother. Her grandmother was quite the character. She used to travel all over the Middle East in the sixties. She brought back all sorts of things—rugs, copper tea sets, these beautiful hand-painted ceramic tiles. We have the tiles set up in the guest bathroom now. It took me three weekends to grout them properly because I insisted on doing it myself instead of hiring a contractor. I watched a bunch of YouTube videos, but let me tell you, grouting is not as easy as those guys make it look. You have to get the consistency just right, like peanut butter, otherwise it just slumps out of the joints...

But, uh, what was the question? Anxious without a reason? Yeah, no. Like I said, there's always something I'm worrying about if I feel that way.
Do you feel anxious when you're doing something you enjoy, like playing your guitar?

Playing my guitar? Well, um, I try to enjoy it, but honestly... what actually finally pushed me to come in and see you is that my shoulders and neck just stay completely clenched all day. It's like I'm constantly bracing for a classroom observation that never ends, you know? And by the evening, my jaw aches so badly from clenching it that I can hardly even enjoy playing. 

I've got this beautiful old Martin acoustic. I bought it second-hand from a guy who used to play in a bluegrass band back in the seventies. He had all these stories about touring up and down the East Coast in a beat-up Ford Econoline van. He said they once played a gig at a county fair where the stage was literally built over a pig pen, and the smell was so bad the banjo player passed out halfway through their set. I don't know if I believe him, but it's a great story. He kept the guitar in pristine condition, though. The action on it is just perfect. I use these medium gauge phosphor bronze strings, which give it this really warm, rich tone. It takes a toll on your calluses, though, let me tell you. If you don't play every day, your fingertips get soft, and then it hurts like crazy to hold down a chord. 

I was trying to teach myself this James Taylor fingerpicking pattern last night, but like I said, my jaw was just throbbing, and my neck felt like a block of cement. I couldn't even focus on the music. I just ended up putting it back in the case. The case is lined with this crushed green velvet, which smells faintly of old pipe tobacco. It's actually a really comforting smell, reminds me of my grandfather... 

But yeah, playing guitar. I want to enjoy it, but I'm just so tense all the time lately.
Do you think your anxiety would completely go away if your work situation and teaching concerns were fully resolved?

Would it go away? I... I don't know. Honestly, I don't think it would. Even if all the school stuff was fixed right now, my mind just... it just keeps circling. Like, I worry about whether I'll ever get hired again, or if I've completely ruined my reputation with the parents. And then it jumps to whether my retirement is slipping away. It gets so bad I start thinking about whether a tiny mistake I made during a story-time activity means I shouldn't even be trusted with children anymore. 

We were reading *Where the Wild Things Are* last week. It's a classic, you know? Maurice Sendak. Did you know he originally wanted to draw horses, but he couldn't get them right, so he drew "wild things" instead? Anyway, I completely skipped a page—the one where Max makes mischief of one kind and another. Little Leo noticed immediately, of course. He pointed it out in front of the whole class. He’s got this booming little voice for a five-year-old. His parents are both theater actors, actually. They do a lot of local productions down at the community playhouse. I went to see them in *Our Town* a few years ago. It was a really good production, although the seating in that theater is terrible. It's all these old wooden folding chairs that squeak every time you shift your weight. By the third act, my back was absolutely killing me. I had to go to a chiropractor for three weeks after that just to get my spine aligned again. The chiropractor had this machine that looked like a medieval torture device... 

Wait, what did you ask me? If the anxiety would stop? Yeah, no, I just... my brain always finds something else to spin out about. It never really stops.
Do you think you would feel anxious if you were not a teacher and had no involvement with schools?

If I wasn't a teacher? Wow, um... I really don't know. I honestly can't even picture it. I've been in early education for so long... if I had no involvement with schools at all, I'm not sure what I'd even do. Maybe something with plants? I've always loved gardening. I have this incredible Monstera plant out in my sunroom. It's huge now. I actually got it at this little estate sale about three years ago. The woman running the sale was clearing out her mother's house, and she had this massive collection of vintage watering cans. Just dozens of them lined up on the driveway. They were mostly galvanized steel, a lot of them imported from England back in the day. I ended up buying one with this really long spout because it's perfect for reaching the back row of pots without spilling water everywhere. 

The problem with the sunroom, though, is the morning glare. It gets so intensely hot in there by 10 AM that the leaves on my plants can actually scorch if I don't pull the shades down. They're these bamboo roll-up shades. I had to special order them from a catalog because the windows are completely non-standard sizes. The whole house was built in 1924, so nothing is standard. Don't even get me started on the plumbing. Last winter, we had a pipe burst in the basement right next to the water heater, and the plumber who came out said the pipes were so old they practically crumbled when he put a wrench to them. It cost an absolute fortune to fix, and he tracked mud all over the basement stairs. I spent three hours scrubbing the wood with Murphy's Oil Soap, which has a nice smell, but it's really tough on your knees when you're down there scrubbing...

But, um... sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, not being a teacher. Yeah, I don't know. Even if I was just watering plants for a living, I feel like my brain would just find something else to obsess over, honestly.

patient.answer: Well, honestly, what finally pushed me to come in is... my shoulders and neck just stay clenched all day. It's like I'm constantly bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. You have to get the consistency just right, like peanut butter, otherwise it just slumps out of the joints...

But, uh, what was the question? Anxious without a reason? Yeah, no. Like I said, there's always something I'm worrying about if I feel that way.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences anxiety in their free time
doctor.question: Do you feel anxious when you're doing something you enjoy, like playing your guitar?

target_item.name: Muscle_Tension
target_item.manifestation: Honestly, what finally pushed me to come in is that my shoulders and neck stay clenched all day, like I'm bracing for a classroom observation that never ends, and by evening my jaw aches so badly I can hardly enjoy playing guitar.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question about playing the guitar directly connects to the patient's manifestation of muscle tension, where his jaw aches so badly by the evening that he can hardly enjoy playing his guitar.

patient.answer:
Playing my guitar? Well, um, I try to enjoy it, but honestly... what actually finally pushed me to come in and see you is that my shoulders and neck just stay completely clenched all day. It's like I'm constantly bracing for a classroom observation that never ends, you know? And by the evening, my jaw aches so badly from clenching it that I can hardly even enjoy playing. 

I've got this beautiful old Martin acoustic. I bought it second-hand from a guy who used to play in a bluegrass band back in the seventies. He had all these stories about touring up and down the East Coast in a beat-up Ford Econoline van. He said they once played a gig at a county fair where the stage was literally built over a pig pen, and the smell was so bad the banjo player passed out halfway through their set. I don't know if I believe him, but it's a great story. He kept the guitar in pristine condition, though. The action on it is just perfect. I use these medium gauge phosphor bronze strings, which give it this really warm, rich tone. It takes a toll on your calluses, though, let me tell you. If you don't play every day, your fingertips get soft, and then it hurts like crazy to hold down a chord. 

I was trying to teach myself this James Taylor fingerpicking pattern last night, but like I said, my jaw was just throbbing, and my neck felt like a block of cement. I couldn't even focus on the music. I just ended up putting it back in the case. The case is lined with this crushed green velvet, which smells faintly of old pipe tobacco. It's actually a really comforting smell, reminds me of my grandfather... 

But yeah, playing guitar. I want to enjoy it, but I'm just so tense all the time lately.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's anxiety is better explained by a generalized anxiety disorder or an adjustment disorder
doctor.question: Do you think your anxiety would completely go away if your work situation and teaching concerns were fully resolved?

target_item.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
target_item.manifestation: My mind keeps circling from whether I'll ever get hired again to whether I've ruined my reputation with parents, whether retirement is slipping away, and even whether a small mistake in a story-time activity means I shouldn't be trusted with children anymore.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the anxiety is restricted only to work-related concerns, which probes whether the worry spans a number of events or activities as described in Excessive Anxiety/Worry.

patient.answer:
Would it go away? I... I don't know. Honestly, I don't think it would. Even if all the school stuff was fixed right now, my mind just... it just keeps circling. Like, I worry about whether I'll ever get hired again, or if I've completely ruined my reputation with the parents. And then it jumps to whether my retirement is slipping away. It gets so bad I start thinking about whether a tiny mistake I made during a story-time activity means I shouldn't even be trusted with children anymore. 

We were reading *Where the Wild Things Are* last week. It's a classic, you know? Maurice Sendak. Did you know he originally wanted to draw horses, but he couldn't get them right, so he drew "wild things" instead? Anyway, I completely skipped a page—the one where Max makes mischief of one kind and another. Little Leo noticed immediately, of course. He pointed it out in front of the whole class. He’s got this booming little voice for a five-year-old. His parents are both theater actors, actually. They do a lot of local productions down at the community playhouse. I went to see them in *Our Town* a few years ago. It was a really good production, although the seating in that theater is terrible. It's all these old wooden folding chairs that squeak every time you shift your weight. By the third act, my back was absolutely killing me. I had to go to a chiropractor for three weeks after that just to get my spine aligned again. The chiropractor had this machine that looked like a medieval torture device... 

Wait, what did you ask me? If the anxiety would stop? Yeah, no, I just... my brain always finds something else to spin out about. It never really stops.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's anxiety is exclusively related to work or teaching
doctor.question: Do you think you would feel anxious if you were not a teacher and had no involvement with schools?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking a hypothetical question to determine if the anxiety is strictly limited to the patient's profession (teaching), which is a differential diagnostic question. The symptom profile does not contain a specific item that answers this, as Excessive Anxiety/Worry was already addressed.

patient.answer:
If I wasn't a teacher? Wow, um... I really don't know. I honestly can't even picture it. I've been in early education for so long... if I had no involvement with schools at all, I'm not sure what I'd even do. Maybe something with plants? I've always loved gardening. I have this incredible Monstera plant out in my sunroom. It's huge now. I actually got it at this little estate sale about three years ago. The woman running the sale was clearing out her mother's house, and she had this massive collection of vintage watering cans. Just dozens of them lined up on the driveway. They were mostly galvanized steel, a lot of them imported from England back in the day. I ended up buying one with this really long spout because it's perfect for reaching the back row of pots without spilling water everywhere. 

The problem with the sunroom, though, is the morning glare. It gets so intensely hot in there by 10 AM that the leaves on my plants can actually scorch if I don't pull the shades down. They're these bamboo roll-up shades. I had to special order them from a catalog because the windows are completely non-standard sizes. The whole house was built in 1924, so nothing is standard. Don't even get me started on the plumbing. Last winter, we had a pipe burst in the basement right next to the water heater, and the plumber who came out said the pipes were so old they practically crumbled when he put a wrench to them. It cost an absolute fortune to fix, and he tracked mud all over the basement stairs. I spent three hours scrubbing the wood with Murphy's Oil Soap, which has a nice smell, but it's really tough on your knees when you're down there scrubbing...

But, um... sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, not being a teacher. Yeah, I don't know. Even if I was just watering plants for a living, I feel like my brain would just find something else to obsess over, honestly.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of excessive worry about work-related issues, physical tension, and difficulty enjoying activities outside of work due to anxiety are consistent with a diagnosis of Somatoform Disorder, specifically F45.41, which is characterized by persistent and excessive worry about bodily symptoms or health concerns, in this case, the patient's neck and jaw tension.
